v0.13.0·Beta·MIT·Windows and macOS

Heavy CAD, made light enough for a browser.

MeshOptimiser opens a heavy CAD assembly, keeps one copy of every part that repeats, and gives you a small GLB plus a viewer to look around, clean up and export. It’s free, it’s open source, and nothing leaves your computer.

See what is inside

Pull it apart, and look inside.

This is a real mesh, a rear derailleur in 43 parts, and it comes apart as you scroll. In the app every pin, bolt and bushing has its own row, its own triangle count, and a button to hide it, simplify it or take it out.

320 MB → 11 MB
The README’s example: a STEP assembly down to a compressed GLB.

GLBs shrink that much with Meshopt compression, through gltfpack.

Why

A tool for getting heavy CAD assemblies into the browser.

The problem is a practical one. A real STEP file can hold 400 identical bolts, 80 duplicate brackets and half a million broken triangles, and a browser is still expected to draw it. MeshOptimiser reads the assembly, spots the parts that are the same and keeps one mesh with a list of positions, rebuilds the bad geometry, and drops what’s too small to see.

What you get back is a compressed GLB and a viewer to look at it in: the part tree, recolouring, mesh tools, a library of parts to add, and export. It runs on your own machine with Python and a browser, as an open take on what tools like Pixyz do.

What the pipeline collapses
400 bolts × 50 KB→1 mesh × 50 KB + 400 positions
80 brackets × 12 KB→1 mesh × 12 KB + 80 positions
500K broken triangles→Rebuilt, and the tiny ones dropped
320 MB STEP→11 MB compressed GLB

How it works

Three steps from STEP to the browser.

  1. 01

    STEP in

    Drop a .step or .stp file on the start screen, or run the converter from the command line.

  2. 02

    Convert

    OpenCascade reads the whole assembly with its names and colours. Repeated parts become one mesh, surfaces are rebuilt, tiny parts are dropped and the result is compressed.

  3. 03

    GLB out

    Open it in the viewer to look around, recolour, reduce, tidy the tree and export.

In motion

Tools that do one job, and say what it saved.

All features

A closer look

Built for assemblies with thousands of parts.

01

One button, half the triangles

Smart optimise runs every clean-up the app has, in order: empty and broken parts, hidden parts, fasteners, tiny parts, holes in flat faces, and then a reduction to the target you set. On this derailleur it took 1,103,373 triangles down to 552,115 and showed what it had saved. One Ctrl+Z puts it all back.

02

Bolts, found by their shape

Names in a CAD export rarely say what a part is. Fasteners cuts each part across its axis and reads the outline: a round shank with a wider head, six flats around a hole, a flat ring. It finds hex bolts, socket screws, nuts and washers whatever they’re called, and leaves bushings, bearings and O-rings alone. Twelve here, 129,460 triangles.

03

172,894 triangles down to 114

Smart fit used to turn a bracket into a brick. Blocks rebuilds a part from a coarse grid, so its steps, arms and openings stay where they were. Here it took the two heaviest parts of the derailleur from 172,894 triangles to 114.

04

A bolt that brings its own nut

Tick it on, pick the nut and set how far from the head it sits. The nut is part of the bolt’s own shape, in the bolt’s thread. It’s one part in the tree and one undo step, and it can’t slide off the end.

The library

Eighty-six parts, one drag away.

Bolts, nuts, pipe fittings, profiles, gears, a stepper motor. Pick a shelf, then drag a part into the scene on the right, or double-click it. In the app each of these is a real part with sizes you can change before it goes in.

Try it

Search is how you get around.

This is the app’s own search, filled with a rear derailleur’s parts. Type a part, a library item or a command. The arrow keys move, Enter runs, and it does sums too.

  • boltThe bolts in the scene and every bolt in the library, in one list.
  • 12*25.4Sums are worked out as you type. Enter copies the answer.
  • 2 inA length in inches comes back in millimetres, which is what the scene uses.
  • fillCommands are in the same list, with their shortcuts.
    ↑↓ choose↵ runEsc clear12*25.4 · 2 in · a part’s name

    Latest release

    v0.13.0

    Full changelog

    It now feels like an app. You can install it, it opens in a window with no address bar or browser tabs, and the title bar can fold away. The scene tabs got better too, and a view that’s moving skips what you couldn’t see anyway.

    • NewInstall it from Chrome or Edge and you get a desktop icon and a window of its own. start.bat opens that window directly.
    • NewIn the installed app you can fold the title bar away. The window buttons float over the corner and the app’s own top bar takes over.
    • NewDrag tabs into order. The tab follows the pointer, the others slide aside, and Esc puts it back.
    • PolishTabs have a dot on the icon (yellow for unsaved, green for saved), a click on the icon saves, and the close button moved to the right end.

    Run it on your own machine.

    Free and open source under the MIT licence. Windows and macOS; your files never leave the computer.
